title: Joseph Trusted, Tempted, and Framed
overview: Sold as a slave in Egypt, Joseph rises to run his master's house, refuses his master's wife, is falsely accused, and is thrown into prison, where he is trusted again.

parts.label: Rising in Potiphar's house (vv. 1-6a)
parts.note: Joseph is bought by Potiphar, a high royal official whose exact duties are uncertain, and soon he is managing the whole estate. The story credits this to the LORD being with Joseph, and says the blessing spilled over onto his Egyptian master's household too.

parts.label: Joseph says no (vv. 6b-10)
parts.note: His master's wife keeps asking him to sleep with her, and he refuses, saying it would betray the man who trusted him with everything and would be a sin against God. He refuses day after day and even avoids being near her.

parts.label: The cloak as false evidence (vv. 11-18)
parts.note: When she grabs him and he runs, she keeps his cloak and claims he attacked her, stressing to the servants and her husband that he is a Hebrew, a foreigner with no one to speak for him. This is the second time Joseph's clothing is used to tell a lie about him; earlier his brothers used his robe to fake his death.

parts.label: Into the king's prison (vv. 19-20)
parts.note: Potiphar is furious and puts Joseph in the prison that held the king's own prisoners. Some readers think this was a lighter punishment than such a charge might bring and wonder if Potiphar had doubts, but the text does not say.

parts.label: Trusted again behind bars (vv. 21-23)
parts.note: The pattern repeats: the LORD is with Joseph, and the warden soon puts him in charge of the whole prison. That phrase appears near the chapter's start and again at its end, framing everything unfair in between.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether this chapter is mainly a moral example of resisting temptation or mainly a story about God quietly working through unjust events.
think: When doing the right thing costs a person dearly, what do you think keeps them from giving up?
